where.en: project lead → spun out, solo since

en: TypeScript
React
Postgres
Supabase Realtime
Academic platform for SBU and SUNY Korea students. Sign-up is restricted to @stonybrook.edu addresses. 100 users in the first twenty days, currently on 3.7.1.

GPA visualization and simulation, curriculum paths, your timetable laid over your friends', anonymous course reviews, cafés near campus, and so on. First version updated by polling, later migrated to Supabase Realtime.

Started October 2025 as a joint Decompiler × LAMBDA club project. I did idea generation and ran it as project leader with a team of 12. Split off as an independent project in January 2026 and still running.
ko: SBU & SUNYK 학생들을 위한 학사 플랫폼. 서비스는 @stonybrook.edu 도메인으로만 적용됨. 첫 20일에 가입자 100명 달성, 현재 v.3.7.1 버전
학점 시각화 및 시뮬레이션, 커리큘럼 경로, 친구 시간표 위에 겹쳐 보는 내 시간표, 익명 강의평, 그리고 학교 근처 카페 등등등등 제공; 첫 버전은 폴링으로 갱신했고 Supabase Realtime으로 migration함
2025년 10월, Decompiler × LAMBDA 동아리 합동 프로젝트로 시작했고 idea generation 및 project leader을 맡아 12명의 팀으로 시작함. 2026년 1월에 독립 프로젝트로 떨어져 나왔고 현재 또한 계속해서 진행중

lede.en: Twenty tables, one upload, and a lot of arguing with myself about how much to show a student at once.
lede.ko: 테이블 스무 개, 업로드 한 번. 학생한테 한 화면에 얼마나 보여줄지를 제일 오래 고민했음.

en: The whole thing hangs off one action: you upload a transcript, and everything after that is derived. GPA simulation, what a curriculum path costs you, which requirements are already closed out. About twenty tables in Postgres holding it up.

The first version polled. It worked while there were thirty people on it. Timetables are the part where two people are looking at the same thing at the same time, so polling showed its age fast — you would drag a block and your friend saw it half a minute later. Moving to Supabase Realtime took a weekend and removed a whole category of complaint.

Restricting sign-up to @stonybrook.edu was not a security decision. It keeps the course reviews attached to people who actually took the course, which is the only reason anonymous reviews are worth reading.

Running it as a 12-person club project and running it alone are different jobs. As PL most of my time went to splitting work into pieces that could be finished by someone I could not sit next to. Since January it has been closer to maintenance plus whatever I feel like adding, which is faster and lonelier.
ko: 전체가 동작 하나에 걸려 있음. 성적표를 한 번 올리면 그 뒤는 전부 거기서 파생됨. 학점 시뮬레이션, 커리큘럼 경로별 부담, 이미 채운 요건. Postgres 테이블 스무 개 정도가 이걸 받치고 있음.
첫 버전은 폴링이었음. 사용자가 서른 명일 때는 문제 없었음. 근데 시간표는 두 사람이 같은 걸 동시에 보는 화면이라 폴링의 한계가 금방 드러남. 블록을 옮기면 친구 화면에는 30초쯤 뒤에 반영되는 식. Supabase Realtime으로 옮기는 데 주말 하나 썼고, 그걸로 불만 한 종류가 통째로 사라졌음.
가입을 @stonybrook.edu로 막은 건 보안 때문이 아님. 강의평을 실제로 그 수업을 들은 사람한테 붙여두기 위한 것. 익명 강의평이 읽을 가치가 있으려면 그거 하나는 있어야 함.
12명짜리 동아리 프로젝트로 굴리는 것과 혼자 굴리는 건 다른 일이었음. PL일 때는 옆에 앉아 있지 않은 사람이 끝낼 수 있는 단위로 일을 쪼개는 데 시간이 제일 많이 갔음. 1월 이후로는 유지보수 + 하고 싶은 거 추가에 가까움. 빠르고, 대신 혼자임.

en: SQL
document store
customs flow

Matching Korean sellers with overseas buyers, with customs and shipping paperwork handled inside the platform instead of over email or WhatsApp. Transactions in SQL, high-volume behavioral data in a document store. I work on it in the gaps.
ko: 국내 셀러와 해외 바이어 매칭 및 통관물류 자동화 시스템 개발. 통관과 선적 서류를 이메일 또는 WhatsApp이 아니라 자동화 플랫폼에서 처리함. 거래는 SQL, 양이 많은 행동 데이터는 도큐먼트 스토어;

en: The interesting problem is not the matching. It is that a single shipment produces a dozen documents, each one owned by a different party, each one blocking the next step, and almost all of it currently moves as email attachments.

So the data model is split: the transaction itself is relational and boring on purpose, and the behavioral data — every view, every quote request, every document state change — goes to a document store where the volume does not hurt anything.
It has no launch date. It gets whatever hours are left over, which some months is zero.
ko: 어려운 쪽은 매칭이 아님. 선적 한 건에 서류가 열 개 넘게 붙고, 각각 주체가 다르고, 하나가 막히면 다음이 안 넘어가는데, 지금은 그게 거의 다 이메일 첨부로 돌아간다는 것.
그래서 데이터 모델을 갈랐음. 거래 자체는 관계형으로, 일부러 심심하게. 조회·견적 요청·서류 상태 변경 같은 행동 데이터는 양이 많아도 상관없는 도큐먼트 스토어로.
출시일 없음. 남는 시간에만 함. 어떤 달은 0시간.

Offline tool for internal use. Under NDA, so that is as far as it goes.
ko: 내부에서 쓰는 오프라인 툴 개발; NDA

lede.en: Four months, one NDA, and a hard requirement I had never had before: no network.

en: I cannot describe what it does. What I can say is that "offline" turned out to be the whole design constraint rather than a deployment detail — no hosted database, no auth service, no calling anything, no assuming a second machine exists.
Most of what I reach for by default assumes a network. Taking that away removed the shortcuts and left the actual problem, which was a good four months.

That meant the parts of an event that are not the event: who had to be contacted, what the space cost and when it was free, and the order everything had to happen in beforehand.
Odoo
Python
scoping

Ran several Odoo implementations at once — scope, schedule, and the constant negotiation between what a client wanted this month and what the team could actually ship. Less code than I expected. More useful than I expected.
ko: Odoo를 활용해 물류통관 업계에서 오프라인으로 이루어지고 있는 업무들을 타겟으로, Odoo를 메인으로 커스터마이징한 프로덕트를 개발하고 해당 내용을 바탕으로 제품설계 및 개발 역할을 진행함.

lede.en: Six months of finding out that scoping is the engineering.

en: Odoo covers most of what a mid-size company needs out of the box. The work is almost never "build this feature" — it is working out whether the client's request is a config change, a small module, or a demand that the product be something it is not. Getting that wrong in week one costs you month three.
Running several at the same time meant the failure mode was never technical. It was two clients both expecting the same week from the same two people.
I wrote less Python than I wanted to. I got much better at saying what something would cost before agreeing to it.

As vice president I mostly scheduled things and noticed who had gone quiet. As president the job was making sure somebody other than me could answer the questions, which is slower and much less satisfying in the moment.
SeekOnce came out of this club, which is the strongest argument I have for it existing.
The SBU chapter starts in fall 2026 and I am starting it from zero again.
booking
scheduling
Reservation site for school facilities, run for high schools. Nine months. Building it and keeping it running turned out to be two different jobs.
ko: 학교 시설을 예약하는 사이트를 만들어 고등학교를 대상으로 운영했다.

lede.en: Nine months, and about seven of them were operations.

en: Booking looks like a solved problem until you meet double-booking, cancellations that arrive after the slot started, and a teacher who wants the gym every Tuesday forever.
The build was maybe two months. The rest was answering the phone, fixing the thing someone did that I had not imagined anyone doing, and learning that a system nobody maintains stops being a system.
First time I ran something other people depended on to get through a normal week.

JavaScript

The student application process was on paper. Moved it to the web with PHP, HTML and JavaScript, drew the mobile and desktop layouts, deployed on Cafe24 including the server config.
ko: 학생 지원 절차가 모두 오프라인 형식인 데에 착안하여, PHP, HTML, JavaScript로 웹에 옮기고 모바일·데스크톱 레이아웃 작업, 서버 설정 포함해서 카페24에 배포

lede.en: My first paid work, and the first time I touched a server that other people were already using.

en: Paper applications meant someone was retyping every form into a spreadsheet. That is the entire brief.

PHP on Cafe24 is not a stack anyone would pick today, and I do not regret the two years. Shared hosting teaches you where the edges are — what you can install, what you cannot, what happens at 9am when everybody submits at once.
Drawing the mobile layout mattered more than anything else I did. Almost every applicant filled the form on a phone.
product
pitch
Planned the product and gave the final pitch: an AI platform for capturing know-how inside small manufacturers before the people holding it retire. First place overall.
ko: 제품을 기획하고 최종 발표를 맡았다. 중소 제조업의 노하우를, 그것을 쥔 사람들이 은퇴하기 전에 물려주는 AI 플랫폼으로 피칭을 진행했고 최종 1위 달성

lede.en: The pitch was the product, for about 48 hours.

en: The premise: in a lot of small Korean manufacturers, the person who knows why a machine is set the way it is has been there thirty years and is about to leave. Nothing is written down, and the reason nothing is written down is that writing it down is a second job.
So the product was about capture with as close to zero effort as possible, and the demo had to make that obvious in three minutes.
I did the planning and the final presentation. First out of every team.
Odoo
project leadership
Odoo's PLO track, finished on the 11th. Also have viewer access to the Odoo Enterprise repository.

lede.en: A certificate that matched work I was already doing.

en: PLO is Odoo's track for the person who owns an implementation end to end rather than a single module — scoping, phasing, and the part where you tell a client no.
I took it while running implementations at DX Tech, so most of it read as a formalization of things I had already gotten wrong once.

tools.en: TypeScript, React and Postgres most days, Supabase when I want to move fast. A couple of years of PHP before that. Odoo, and enough Python to keep it in line. Tailwind because I am faster in it.
